newsitem.title: USA: Calif. legislative panel approves marijuana center.
newsitem.headline: Calif. legislative panel approves marijuana center.

text.p: A state legislative panel Wednesday approved a bill to set up a state-funded center to study the medical uses of marijuana, lawmakers said.
The legislation, by state Senator John Vasconcellos, a Democrat, would also create a task force to draw up a statewide plan to distribute marijuana to those who need it for medical reasons.

After hearing testimony in Sacramento Wednesday, the state Senate Health and Human Services Committee approved the measure on a 5-2 vote, giving the bill its first legislative victory before sending it to another state panel for review.

The bill is aimed at clarifying and putting into effect Proposition 215, a measure passed by California voters last November that allows sick people to legally use marijuana to ease the pain of illnesses such as AIDS, cancer and glaucoma.
The Clinton administration opposed Proposition 215 and has threatened to sanction doctors who prescribe marijuana, which remains an illegal drug under federal law.
Vasconcellos has accused the Clinton administration of avoiding research that might find that marijuana could be a safe and effective medicine.
"We owe it to the people of California to find out under what circumstances marijuana works as medicine," Vasconcellos said at Wednesday's hearing.

His bill would require the University of California to set up a medical marijuana research center to study the medical safety and efficacy of marijuana and develop medical guidelines for its use. It calls for the center to receive $6 million in state funding over three years.
